name: Chatterbug SMTP Email Connector
author: Sam Gazal

sections.description:
Chatterbug SMTP is a lightweight, free WordPress SMTP plugin that allows your website to send emails using Gmail, Amazon SES, your own email account or any SMTP email service instead of relying on hosting service or the default WordPress/PHP mail system.

Connect your WordPress website to Gmail, Google Workspace, Amazon Simple Email Service (SES), or virtually any SMTP-compatible email provider.

Whether your website sends contact form notifications, registration emails, password reset messages, WooCommerce order notifications, or other WordPress emails, Chatterbug SMTP helps route those emails through your chosen email provider.

You remain in control of your email account, SMTP credentials, and email delivery service.

No mandatory subscriptions, no email delivery fees charged by Chatterbug, and no requirement to use an external Chatterbug email service.

Key Features

  • Free to use.
  • Send WordPress emails through your own SMTP server.
  • Gmail and Google Workspace support.
  • Amazon SES SMTP support.
  • Compatible with virtually any SMTP email provider.
  • Support for custom SMTP servers and ports.
  • SMTP authentication with username and password.
  • SSL and TLS encryption options.
  • Configure your sender email address.
  • Configure your sender name.
  • Works with WordPress wp_mail().
  • Works with contact form plugins.
  • Works with WooCommerce email notifications.
  • Supports WordPress registration and password reset emails.
  • Site-wide email delivery configuration.
  • No mandatory third-party email service.
  • Your SMTP credentials remain under your control.

Supported Email Providers

Chatterbug SMTP supports SMTP-compatible email services, including:

  • Gmail
  • Google Workspace
  • Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)
  • Microsoft 365 SMTP
  • Outlook SMTP
  • Yahoo Mail SMTP
  • Zoho Mail
  • SendGrid SMTP
  • Mailgun SMTP
  • Brevo SMTP
  • Custom SMTP servers provided by your hosting company or email provider.

Provider-specific authentication requirements may apply. For example, Gmail and Google Workspace may require an app password or an OAuth-based authentication method, depending on your account configuration.

Configuration

Gmail and Google Workspace

  1. Open Chatterbug SMTP in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Enter the Gmail or Google Workspace SMTP server information.
  3. Configure the required authentication credentials.
  4. Select the appropriate TLS or SSL encryption option.
  5. Save your settings.
  6. Send a test email.

Gmail SMTP settings typically use:

  • SMTP Host: smtp.gmail.com
  • TLS Port: 587
  • SSL Port: 465
  • Authentication: Required

Depending on your Google account security settings, you may need to configure an app password or another supported authentication method.

Amazon SES

  1. Sign in to your AWS account.
  2. Configure Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) in your AWS region.
  3. Obtain your SES SMTP credentials.
  4. Open Chatterbug SMTP in WordPress.
  5. Enter your Amazon SES SMTP endpoint.
  6. Enter your SMTP username and password.
  7. Configure the appropriate port and TLS encryption.
  8. Save your settings and send a test email.

Note: Your Amazon SES account must be properly configured, and your sending domain or email address must be verified. AWS sending restrictions and sandbox limitations may apply.

Custom SMTP Provider

You can connect to virtually any SMTP-compatible email provider.

You will generally need:

  • SMTP hostname
  • SMTP port
  • Encryption method (None, SSL, or TLS)
  • SMTP username
  • SMTP password
  • Sender email address
  • Sender name

Contact your email hosting provider if you need help obtaining these settings.

External Services

Chatterbug SMTP does not require a connection to Chatterbug servers.

The plugin connects to the SMTP provider configured by the website administrator to send WordPress emails.

Depending on the selected provider, email data may be transmitted to:

  • Gmail / Google Workspace SMTP servers.
  • Amazon Simple Email Service SMTP endpoints.
  • Microsoft, Yahoo, Zoho, or other SMTP providers.
  • Custom SMTP servers configured by the website administrator.

Emails sent through these providers are subject to their respective privacy policies and terms of service.

The plugin does not require an external Chatterbug account or subscription.
sections.installation:
1. Install Chatterbug SMTP from the WordPress.org plugin directory or upload the plugin ZIP file through Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Chatterbug SMTP.
  3. Navigate to Chatterbug SMTP in your WordPress administration menu.
  4. Enter your SMTP hostname, port, encryption method, username, and password as required.
  5. Configure your sender email address and sender name.
  6. Save your settings.
  7. Send a test email to verify your configuration.

Once configured, WordPress emails will be sent using your selected SMTP provider.
sections.faq:
Is Chatterbug SMTP free?

Yes. Chatterbug SMTP is free to install and use. There are no mandatory subscriptions or email delivery fees charged by Chatterbug. Your chosen SMTP provider may charge its own fees.

Does Chatterbug SMTP support Gmail?

Yes. You can configure Gmail or Google Workspace as your outgoing email provider using Gmail SMTP settings and the authentication method supported by your Google account.

Does Chatterbug SMTP support Amazon SES?

Yes. You can connect your WordPress website to Amazon SES using your AWS SMTP endpoint and SES SMTP credentials.

Can I use my hosting company’s SMTP server?

Yes. Chatterbug SMTP supports custom SMTP servers, including those provided by your website hosting company.

Does it work with contact form plugins?

Yes. Chatterbug SMTP works with WordPress email delivery through the standard wp_mail() function. Most WordPress contact form plugins use this function to send notifications.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce uses WordPress email functionality, so its transactional emails can be routed through your configured SMTP provider.

Does Chatterbug SMTP replace my email hosting provider?

No. Chatterbug SMTP connects WordPress to your existing email provider. You still need an email account or SMTP service to send messages.

Do I need a Chatterbug account?

No. You do not need a Chatterbug account to use Chatterbug SMTP.

Does Chatterbug SMTP send emails through Chatterbug servers?

No. The plugin is designed to send emails directly through the SMTP provider you configure. Chatterbug does not need to act as an intermediary email delivery service.

Are my SMTP credentials shared with Chatterbug?

No. SMTP credentials are configured and stored on your own WordPress website. They are not sent to Chatterbug servers.

How can I test my SMTP configuration?

Use the test email functionality in the plugin settings to verify that your SMTP connection and authentication are working correctly.

Can I use any SMTP port?

Yes. You can configure the SMTP port provided by your email service, subject to your hosting provider’s network restrictions.

  • Support for Gmail and Google Workspace.
  • Support for Amazon SES.
  • Support for custom SMTP providers.
  • Configurable sender name and email address.
  • SMTP authentication and encryption settings.
  • Test email functionality.
